s1.syndrome_frame: Persistent vertical misalignment with elevation deficit
salient_findings: Elevation deficit of the right eye
Anomalous band in the right orbit
Right orbital linear soft-tissue lesion medial to the medial rectus muscle
key_facts: 52-year-old woman
History of long-standing diplopia
Persistent vertical misalignment
Orthotropic in primary position
Elevation deficit of the right eye
Previous MRI of the orbits revealed an anomalous band in the right orbit
Surgical excision of the anomalous band did not improve motility
MRI of the orbits with and without gadolinium showed a right orbital linear soft-tissue lesion
The lesion was medial to the medial rectus muscle and parallel to it
The lesion had enhancement and signal-intensity characteristics identical to those of extraocular muscle
The globes were unremarkable with no measured proptosis
The retroocular fat, optic nerves and sheaths, optic chiasm, and brain parenchyma appeared normal

shortlist.label: Accessory extraocular muscle
shortlist.why_kept: MRI findings of a right orbital linear soft-tissue lesion with characteristics identical to extraocular muscle, consistent with clinical presentation of persistent vertical misalignment and elevation deficit

shortlist.label: Brown's syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of elevation deficit and previous history of anomalous band in the right orbit, which could be related to a congenital condition affecting the superior oblique tendon

shortlist.label: Duane syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: History of long-standing diplopia and orthotropic in primary position, with elevation deficit, which could be indicative of a congenital condition affecting the extraocular muscles

shortlist.label: Thyroid ophthalmopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Although the globes were unremarkable, thyroid ophthalmopathy can cause restrictive myopathy leading to vertical misalignment, and the patient's age and sex make this a plausible consideration

shortlist.label: Orbital fibrosis
shortlist.why_kept: Previous surgical excision of an anomalous band and the presence of a linear soft-tissue lesion on MRI, which could be consistent with fibrotic changes in the orbit

raw.rationale: The presence of a right orbital linear soft-tissue lesion medial to the medial rectus muscle, parallel to it, with enhancement and signal-intensity characteristics identical to those of extraocular muscle, supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Brown's syndrome
rejected.why: Typically presents with limited elevation in adduction, not a primary finding in this case

rejected.label: Duane syndrome
rejected.why: Characterized by limited horizontal eye movement, not the primary issue here

rejected.label: Thyroid ophthalmopathy
rejected.why: Usually associated with proptosis, periorbital swelling, and other signs not mentioned in the vignette

rejected.label: Orbital fibrosis
rejected.why: Would likely cause more restrictive symptoms and signs, not specifically mentioned
